title: api.v1: the plugin API's entry points, as plain data ('csl-plugin-api/1')
description: SKELETON DRAFT: the lanes that host plugins and draw the page supply the shapes and the fixtures; this file states what holds whatever those shapes become. A plugin gives the daemon plain values and imports nothing from it. Its entry points: registry(), operator() and bind_core() as today; commands(), tools(), on_event(), themes and layouts, and a run the plugin owns, each behind its own appended permission and ignored without it. Nothing here is a record on its own; each definition is what one entry point returns or takes. FROZEN WITH THIS FILE, because nothing else states it: (1) every call a plugin makes into the core carries the principal {kind: plugin, id}, set by the host and never by the plugin ($defs/call_context); (2) on_event names the event types it subscribes to, receives engine output only as untrusted text, and never receives an approval's private binding; (3) a plugin's command or tool is reachable only through the one dispatcher, plugin.call; (4) a run a plugin owns has that plugin as its owner, set by the host, and its effects pass the same approval gate as any other; (5) a theme or a layout never reaches the approval area.

name.description: A name a plugin gives to a command, a tool, a theme or a layout: lower-case letters, digits, '_' and '-', starting with a letter.

call_context.description: What the host attaches to every call a plugin makes into the core. The plugin cannot set or change it.

registry.description: What registry() returns today, with the 'panel' permission: the plugin's panels and what they require. The shape of a panel is the page lane's and goes through the page's own validation.

command.description: One entry of what commands() returns, with the 'command' permission: a command a user can run through plugin.call.

tool.description: One entry of what tools() returns, with the 'tool' permission: a tool declared as data. input_schema is a JSON Schema for the tool's input. A call of it waits in the approval queue like any other effect.

subscription.description: What a plugin declares for on_event, with the 'subscribe' permission: the event types it asks for, by their names in the control records' event schema. The approval types can be asked for; what is delivered for them is the public view, never the private binding.

surface.description: One theme or layout a plugin offers, with the 'surface' permission. The page lane supplies what a theme and a layout hold; neither ever reaches the approval area.

run_request.description: What a plugin passes to start a run it owns, with the 'run' permission. The host adds the principal and the owner; a request that tries to name either is refused.
